page: Amazon Web Services hpc7a.24xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server optimized for high-performance computing workloads. It features 48 dedicated physical cores powered by an AMD EPYC 9R14 processor running at 3.7 GHz, with a single thread per core configuration. The system is equipped with 768.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, providing 16.0 GB of RAM per core. It operates on the Nitro hypervisor, lacks local storage, and includes a baseline network bandwidth of 150 Gbps. No GPUs are bundled with this instance.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier multi-core CPU performance, placing in the top 10% of tested systems. The memory subsystem delivers exceptional throughput, with uncached large-block read bandwidth reaching 695.05 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 347.3 GB/sec, both ranking in the top 10%. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, software compilation with Clang, and Passmark CPU physics tests also demonstrate top-tier performance. Single-core execution and database operations score in the top 25%, while static web serving and gzip compression perform at average levels.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the hpc7a.24xlarge offers high resource density, combining a high-speed dedicated CPU architecture with a massive DDR5 memory footprint. The absence of local storage and GPU hardware makes it a highly specialized resource, avoiding the cost overhead of unused accelerators. This profile is highly suited for compute-heavy and memory-bound workloads such as high-performance computing, scientific simulations, large-scale software compilation, multi-threaded data processing, and Redis-based in-memory database operations.
